title: MOOV Web
subtitle: A website redesign for a new wave of users
thumbnailDescription: Website redesign for a new wave of users.

sections.heading: About the project
sections.role: UX & UI design, UX research and handoff to development.

sections.heading: The challenges
sections.overviewBody: MOOV was transitioning to a second fase of the product, from web to a native app, the new website needs to be a place for new users to explore MOOV's value, answer common questions and ultimately lead them to download the new app.

items.title: Challenge 1
items.description: Design a user experience that inform users what MOOV is about and the platform change.

items.title: Challenge 2
items.description: Take on from the current brand and app UI design, and create a unified product.

items.title: Challenge 3
items.description: Introduce new Enterprise feature as a new product from MOOV.

cards.title: Complete UX redesign
cards.description: With updated information architecture. Tailored for existing and new users.

cards.title: All new interaction design elements
cards.description: Fresh UI elements that unifies both ends of the product, and provides a clear path to complete the task (download app).

leftCard.title: Competition
leftCard.description: I looked into platforms with similar goals and products like:

rightCards.title: Data analysis
rightCards.description: Understanding of who the users are and how the product has evolved since launch.

rightCards.title: User surveys
rightCards.description: I did a surveys on 10 MOOV users from different ages, locations and lifestyles.

cards.title: Where users come from
cards.description: Most users come from recommendations from friends or a social media ad.

cards.title: Big brand rewards
cards.description: Users are mainly interested on the big brand rewards, that's what triggers the decision to download the app.

cards.title: A lot of FAQs
cards.description: There was a lot of information that users weren't aware of, it was not available to them.

cards.title: Rewards first
cards.description: Users are largely interested on the rewards more than any other value proposition from the product.

sections.heading: The design
sections.prototypeCaption: Check a live prototype for the mobile version of the website (Open on desktop for better experience)

items.description: I tested the prototype with users from different age ranges.
I asked 3 users to complete 3 small tasks on the website, and at the end, I asked the users were would they find a specific piece of information, so they would navigate naturally.

items.title: Better understanding
items.description: 3 out of 3 users were able to complete the tasks provided and found the information asked for.

items.title: Too quick to click
items.description: On the first version of the product, the CTAs were fixed throughout the screen, this prompted users to click it way to soon without scanning the website first. I placed the CTAs in strategic places for the iterations.

items.title: Faster understanding of the product
items.description: The overall impact of the redesign was that the improved information architecture, which allowed the user to understand and find information faster.

items.title: New methodologies
items.description: I also was able to introduce the development team to agile sprints, and new software for the handoff. This allowed us to really accelerate the project.

items.title: My UX legacy
items.description: In the end, the company went for a different UI design because it aligned with the upcoming app redesign tasked to another design team. But the company was very satisfied with my UX redesign so they applied the new design to my UX design, which I was glad it could be implemented.

cards.title: Challenges along the way
cards.description:
The development team was not used to agile methodologies and the importance of mobile first design, which initially caused some minor delays.
I did short workshops to align the team, explain how would we be working and introduce the new software.

cards.title: Conclusion
cards.description:
I was able to bring light to some of the misinterpreted user pain points and needs, which allowed me to create a much more streamlined product.
Because the UI was not used, some targets were missed only in minor ways.

cards.title: I would love to redesign app
cards.description: The new website has been launched with the alternative UI, but I would love to approach the company in the future for a redesign of the app, to improve on those key user needs and pain points that were discovered during our collaboration.
